pass_a_gloss: Denial/oath abomination; sun refuses worship, speaks as generated fellow-servant awaiting Rom 8 freedom.
pass_b_english: And if 'every evil word is an abomination to the Lord' (Matthew 5:33–34) thy God, how great an abomination must the evil word of denial be deemed, and the evil word of proclaiming another god, and the evil oath — by man's fortune, a thing without substance? When it is set before us, remember him who taught the 'But I say to you, swear not at all.' (Matthew 12:36) For if he who swears by heaven 'slights the throne of God,' (Romans 8:20–21) and he who swears by earth impiously deifies what is called 'the footstool of God's feet,' and he who swears by Jerusalem sins — though it is a city of the great King — and he who swears by his own head offends: how great a sin must swearing by someone's fortune be deemed? Remember then too the 'for every idle word you shall give account in the day of judgment.' (Deuteronomy 17:3) For what other word is so idle as the word in denial? But the enemy will likely wish to outwit us, by whatever means, toward worshiping 'the sun or the moon or all the order from heaven.' (Matthew 4:10) But we shall say that God's Word commanded not these. For in no way must creatures be worshiped, with the Creator present, who endures and cries toward the prayer of all. Nor would the sun itself wish to be worshiped by those of God's portion — likely not by anyone else either — but imitating him who said, 'Why callest thou me good? None is good but one, God, the Father,' (Mark 10:18) it will as it were say to one willing to worship it: 'Why callest thou me God? One is the true God. And why worshipest thou me? For the Lord thy God shalt thou worship, and him only shalt thou serve. I too am generated. Why wilt thou worship the worshiper? For I too worship and serve God and the Father, and, obeying his commands, 'by vanity' I am subjected 'through him who subjected, in hope' — and I shall be freed 'from the slavery of corruption,' now myself bound in a corruptible body, 'into the freedom of the glory of God's children.'
